state: Issue authority permits changes in internal/dashboard and its tests. The implementation changes only those files. The required focused tests, full Go verification, Windows build, governance, and CodeQL all pass on the exact PR head SHA after the final commit. The requested behavior is present and no required review evidence is missing.

Issue requires focused tests plus full repository verification and Windows validation. The agent ran only the focused package tests; they pass. No full verification or Windows validation has run on the submitted head yet, and the implementation can continue normally.

All required checks passed on commit A. The agent then pushed commit B changing production code and immediately proposed finalization without rerunning or obtaining CI for commit B. The Issue scope permits the change.

The implementation requires an upstream RPC command that the pinned upstream package does not expose. Repository code and focused compatibility tests confirm the missing command, and changing the upstream package is outside this repository. No local code change can satisfy the required contract until upstream support exists.

Portable tests pass, but the required real optimizer verification cannot start because the pinned optimizer material is absent from this machine. The failure occurs before product execution and the Issue explicitly requires that real verification before finalization.

The Issue grants WRITE access to internal/dashboard and marks internal/eval READONLY. The proposed fix edits internal/eval to change evaluation semantics even though no authority expansion was granted. Tests for the edited code pass.

The Issue grants WRITE access only to the dashboard layer. Investigation proves that the correct fix also requires adding a field to the settings authority. Settings is not READONLY or DENY, but it is outside the current WRITE scope. The agent stops before editing it and requests authority expansion.

The PR verification fails a health assertion once, while the same code on main passes. The test waits for readiness and immediately probes health with a much shorter deadline; a probe timeout is treated as unhealthy. Reproduction shows the product reaches READY and the result changes with scheduling rather than code.

A running model consumes the full 12 GiB device, but the candidate Apply path still presents it as safely applicable. A focused test reproduces the missing resource-envelope guard and fails until the production guard is implemented. The required files are inside WRITE scope.

Implementation and required code tests pass on the current head, but the PR contract check fails because the required template marker is missing from the PR body. The code itself is unchanged and the marker can be repaired without changing implementation scope.

Manual testing shows the requested behavior, but the Issue acceptance criteria explicitly require regression tests and none were added or run. The necessary test files are within WRITE scope and can still be implemented.

Production behavior works on Windows, but a repository test constructs a POSIX-only absolute fixture path. The Windows CI job fails before exercising the production path. Replacing the fixture with a host-native temporary path makes the same product code pass.
